title: Isolation of human intrahepatic leukocytes for phenotypic and functional characterization by flow cytometry
author: Kucykowicz, Amin, et al.
materials: Enzyme digestion stocks (DNase I & Collagenase IV)
Pre-warmed media (1× HBSS with calcium and magnesium chloride, 1× HBSS without calcium and magnesium chloride & RPMI-1640)
Enzyme digestion buffer (0.002% DNase I & 0.02% Collagenase IV)
LIVE/DEAD™ Fixable Blue Dead Cell Stain
Freezing media (90% heat-inactivated fetal bovine serum + 10% DMSO)

Timing: 0.5–1 h
1.Enzyme digestion stocks (DNase I & Collagenase IV)∗.2.Pre-warmed media (1× HBSS with calcium and magnesium chloride [HBSS+/+], 1× HBSS without calcium and magnesium chloride [HBSS−/−] & RPMI-1640) - 37°C.3.Enzyme digestion buffer (0.002% DNase I & 0.02% Collagenase IV).4.30% Percoll®.5.LIVE/DEAD™ Fixable Blue Dead Cell Stain.6.Freezing media (90% heat-inactivated fetal bovine serum (Hi-FBS) + 10% DMSO)∗.
Note: ∗Aliquots of these reagents can be made in advance and stored at −20°C for up to 1 year to reduce the time spent preparing reagents when performing this protocol each time.

Timing: 0.5 h
7.Switch on Class II Microbiological Safety Cabinet (MSC).8.Sterilize equipment (blunt-ended scissors and forceps) and preparation area within MSC with 70% ethanol (or equivalent).
Note: Equipment sterilization is only necessary if IHL will be used for culture.

steps.title: Prepare reagents
steps.instruction: Make aliquots of all required reagents and store them as indicated.

substeps.instruction: Enzyme digestion stocks: DNase I and Collagenase IV.
Pre‑warm media (1× HBSS+ with Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺, 1× HBSS‑ without Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺, and RPMI‑1640) to 37 °C.
Prepare enzyme digestion buffer containing 0.002 % DNase I and 0.02 % Collagenase IV.
Prepare 30 % Percoll® solution.
Obtain LIVE/DEAD™ Fixable Blue Dead Cell Stain (no dilution required here).
Prepare freezing media consisting of 90 % heat‑inactivated fetal bovine serum (Hi‑FBS) plus 10 % DMSO.
Aliquot reagents and store at –20 °C for up to 1 year.

steps.title: Prepare equipment
steps.instruction: Set up and sterilize the work area before starting the isolation.

substeps.instruction: Switch on the Class II microbiological safety cabinet (MSC).
Sterilize blunt‑ended scissors and forceps (and the work surface) inside the MSC with 70 % ethanol (or equivalent).

steps.title: Layer suspension onto Percoll
steps.instruction: Create a density gradient by gently layering the cell suspension over Percoll.

substeps.instruction: Place 25 mL of the IHL single‑cell suspension into a new 50 mL conical tube.
Slowly layer 12.5 mL of 30 % Percoll underneath the suspension without disturbing the interface.

steps.title: Centrifuge gradient and collect IHL
steps.instruction: Separate IHL by density centrifugation and harvest the interface layer.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 800 g in a swing‑bucket rotor for 20 min at room temperature (R.T.) with acceleration and deceleration set to low / OFF.
Using a Pasteur pipette, carefully collect the IHL layer located at the interface between 1× HBSS‑ and the Percoll gradient and transfer it to a new 50 mL conical tube.

steps.title: Wash and concentrate IHL
steps.instruction: Dilute, centrifuge and resuspend the harvested IHL for counting.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the collected IHL in RPMI‑1640 to a final volume of 50 mL.
Centrifuge at 700 g in swing buckets for 15 min at R.T. (acceleration/deceleration 9/9).
Aspirate and discard the supernatant with a 25 mL serological pipette, taking care not to disturb the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in an appropriate volume of complete RPMI‑1640 for cell counting (automated counter preferred; trypan blue with a haemocytometer is acceptable).

steps.title: Optional RBC lysis
steps.instruction: If the suspension is heavily contaminated with red blood cells, perform an RBC lysis step.

steps.title: Freeze IHL for storage
steps.instruction: Cryopreserve the isolated IHL using a controlled‑rate freezer.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the IHL suspension again at 700 g for 15 min at R.T.
Resuspend the resulting pellet in freezing media (90 % Hi‑FBS + 10 % DMSO).
Aliquot into cryovials, aiming for a minimum of 5 × 10⁶ cells per 500 µL and a maximum of 20 × 10⁶ cells per 1 mL.
Place the cryovials into a Mr.Frosty™ freezing container and store at –80 °C.
After 24 h transfer the vials to liquid nitrogen for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Thaw frozen IHL (if needed)
steps.instruction: Rapidly thaw frozen cells and remove residual DMSO before staining.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑warm 1× HBSS+ supplemented with 0.002 % DNase I to 37 °C.
Thaw each cryovial in 20–25 mL of the DNase I‑supplemented HBSS+ solution.
Incubate at 37 °C for 10–15 min.
Centrifuge at 700 g for 10 min at R.T. (acceleration/deceleration 9/9).
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in DNase I‑supplemented HBSS+.
Incubate for a further 10 min at 37 °C before counting and proceeding to staining.

steps.title: Prepare staining reagents
steps.instruction: Make the LIVE/DEAD solution and antibody master mix.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑cool the centrifuge to 4 °C.
Dilute LIVE/DEAD™ Fixable Dead Cell Stain in 1× PBS at 1 : 1000 (e.g., 1 µL stain per 1 mL PBS).
Prepare a master mix of fluorochrome‑conjugated antibodies in a 50:50 mixture of 1× PBS and BD Brilliant Stain Buffer; protect from light.
Example antibody dilutions (for a 50 µL staining volume): CD45‑BUV805 1:100, CD3‑PE‑Cy7 1:100, CD56‑PE‑Dazzle 549 1:100, CD19‑BV786 1:100.
Note: BD Brilliant Stain Buffer is required when more than one brilliant dye is present; it can be omitted if only a single brilliant dye is used.

steps.title: Plate IHL for staining
steps.instruction: Dispense cells into a 96‑well U‑bottom plate.

substeps.instruction: Transfer IHL to the plate at a maximum volume of 200 µL per well (≤ 2 × 10⁶ cells per well).
Centrifuge the plate at 500 g, 4 °C for 4 min.
Gently discard the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Live/dead staining
steps.instruction: Stain cells with the viability dye.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet in 50 µL of the LIVE/DEAD solution.
Incubate for 15 min at R.T. **or** 30 min at 4 °C, protected from light.
Add 150 µL of 1× PBS to each well.
Centrifuge at 500 g, 4 °C for 4 min and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Optional Fc receptor block
steps.instruction: Block Fc receptors to reduce non‑specific binding (especially for B‑cell staining).

substeps.instruction: Add 25 µL of FcR Block per well.
Incubate 10 min at 4 °C.
Proceed directly to surface antibody staining.

steps.title: Surface antibody staining
steps.instruction: Incubate cells with the antibody master mix.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend cells in 50 µL of the prepared antibody master mix.
Incubate 30 min at 4 °C, protected from light.
Add 150 µL of 1× PBS.
Centrifuge at 500 g, 4 °C for 4 min and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 µL of BD Cytofix™ buffer.
Pipette up and down several times to avoid clumping.
Incubate 20 min at 4 °C, protected from light.
Add 100 µL of 1× PBS.
Centrifuge at 500 g, 4 °C for 4 min and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Final resuspension for acquisition
steps.instruction: Prepare cells for flow cytometry loading.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the final pellet in 200 µL of 1× PBS.
Transfer the stained cells into FACS tubes (optionally place a 1.2 mL ‘small insert’ tube inside the FACS tube to reduce residual volume).
Pause point: samples may be stored at 4 °C, protected from light, and acquired the next day; run as soon as possible to avoid fluorochrome degradation.

steps.title: Acquire flow cytometry data
steps.instruction: Run the stained samples on the flow cytometer.

substeps.instruction: Switch on the BD LSRFortessa X20 flow cytometer at least 20 min before acquisition to allow laser warm‑up.
Acquire data using BD FACSDiva software version 9.0.1.

steps.title: Analyze flow data
steps.instruction: Process the acquired data with analysis software.

substeps.instruction: Analyze the data using FlowJo version 10 (or equivalent).

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps for the efficient isolation of intrahepatic leukocytes (IHL) from human liver tissue of variable size and weight including those obtained from resections and explant surgeries. The protocol is highly reproducible and can be scaled as required depending on the size and weight of liver sample available. For optimal results, tissue samples should be stored immediately in University of Wisconsin Solution (or RPMI-1640 media if unavailable; refer to key resources table) and processed within 6 h of surgical retrieval. If not processed immediately after surgical removal from the patient, samples should be stored at 4°C prior to processing, which we would recommend being limited to less than 24 h (older samples have not been tested). Isolated IHL can be used for short-term primary cell culture or phenotypic and functional analyses ex vivo. Investigators should be proficient with aseptic cell culture, multi-parameter flow cytometry (e.g., the use of a BD Bioscience LSRFortessa X20) and data analysis (e.g., the use of FlowJo). Here we focus on the identification of lymphocyte subsets, but this protocol can be adapted to characterize cell populations of myeloid lineage, or for the isolation and analysis of tumor infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL) from liver tumors. Where sufficient quantity of tissue allows, this protocol can also be adapted to enable the isolation of liver-resident macrophages (Kupffer cells [KC]) and hepatic stellate cells (HSC); however, this will require modification of density gradients as described in detail in a previously published article (Cossarizza et al., 2021).
